correctness.rationale: All masks for each finite n=6..9 are exactly enumerated via the induced maximum-degree<=1 equivalent condition. A deterministic list of vertex-toggle matchings covers all noncritical cells, and every Hasse cover is explicitly tested for acyclicity (809,2268,6710,20799 nonempty faces; 402,1133,3351,10397 pairs). The surviving counts give n=7,8,9 sphere wedges directly. For n=6 the integer Morse 4-to-3 attaching-degree vector is (0,0,0), proved by exhaustive integer signed gradient cancellation; the 2-connected three-skeleton has pi_3 iso H_3 by Hurewicz, so the sole four-cell attaches trivially. No inference beyond n=6..9.

originality.rationale: The exact four intermediate n=6..9 integral homotopy types are not consequences of the accessible adjacent n=5 and n=10 two-independence computations. Full-text comparisons with directly relevant recent arXiv work distinguish shellability and Alexander-dual statements from integral homotopy and from the ordinary independence polynomial on the same graphs. Exact parameter and stronger-coverage search of indexed research yielded no decisive covering result, while unindexed calculations remain a real residual risk.
residual_risks: A special-case higher-independence enumeration in a nonindexed thesis, preprint or graph database may already contain one or more cases.

value.rationale: The contiguous missing four cases of a canonical cubic generalized-Petersen family are a natural finite cutoff between known Petersen n=5 and dodecahedral n=10 boundary examples, rather than arbitrary graph-label slices. The first case has mixed-dimensional integral homotopy with a genuine attaching map whose vanishing must be established; the next three have distinct pure fifth-dimensional wedge ranks. A fully reproducible exact finite benchmark can inform further classification without an unsupported general pattern.
